justification: Close the terrain two-layer timeout gap. The brief's outer terrain collection budget was 80s, but the DEM service's INNER HTTP timeout (_TIMEOUT) was 40s — and SIX Maps (the only working DEM source) is variable, sometimes >40s. So the inner 40s killed the fetch before the outer budget mattered, and terrain still failed when SIX Maps was slow. Raised the inner DEM _TIMEOUT 40->65s (the true reliability limit) and the outer timeout_terrain 80->100s to cover GA(12+12 capped) + SIX(65) + the whitebox chain. Two constants only.

pre_impl.existing_data: dem_service._TIMEOUT bounded each DEM HTTP call (GA capped at 12, SIX at _TIMEOUT); intelligence_brief.CONFIG.timeout_terrain bounded the terrain future.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Raising only the outer collection budget (done earlier) did not help — the inner 40s HTTP timeout on SIX Maps was the binding limit.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Two existing constants bumped; no new mechanism.
pre_impl.external_source_error: SIX Maps slowness now tolerated to 65s; a still-slower response or failure surfaces an honest NOT_AVAILABLE terrain card (unchanged behaviour).
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: terrain could still fail when SIX Maps took 40-65s because the inner timeout fired. After: the inner timeout matches the outer budget so the working source has real room to return.

functions.name: fetch_dem_region
functions.input: lat, lng, buffer_m, and a timeout defaulting to _TIMEOUT (now 65s)
functions.output: a DEM GeoTIFF from GA or SIX Maps with the SIX Maps HTTP call now allowed up to 65s
functions.if_none: raises RuntimeError on failure; the brief maps it to a NOT_AVAILABLE terrain section

values: N/A - timeout constants, not regulatory values.

break_it.what_happens: the DEM fetch times out and terrain shows an honest unavailable card
break_it.repro: hit SIX Maps under heavy load
break_it.how: 65s covers the observed variance; a slower response is genuinely degraded service and surfaces NOT_AVAILABLE, not a fake diagram

break_it.scenario: A 100s terrain budget slows the whole brief
break_it.what_happens: a brief could run up to ~100s when terrain is the slowest layer
break_it.repro: run a brief with satellite on while SIX Maps is slow
break_it.how: layers run concurrently so total = the slowest layer; the user explicitly chose reliability over speed; the concurrency cap (#577) bounds memory

break_it.scenario: GA WCS starts hanging and eats the budget
break_it.what_happens: GA could waste time before SIX Maps runs
break_it.how: GA stays capped at 12s per attempt, so the worst-case before SIX Maps is ~24s, leaving 76s for SIX inside the 100s budget

post_merge.other_repo: N/A - the standalone terrain tool benefits from the same DEM timeout.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run a brief with satellite on for an inner-Sydney address while SIX Maps is responsive: the terrain diagram renders; when SIX Maps is slow (40-65s) it now still completes rather than timing out at 40s.
